title: Unclog long-context queues with preemptive dequeue and backpressure smoothing
creator: Anika Patel
description: Customer escalation from 'Acme Health' reported persistent 95th/99th token latency spikes on the Private deployment when mixed short and long-context workloads coexist. Initial triage showed a repeating pattern: tenant long-context requests would trigger large KV cache retention and cause the adaptive batcher to form very large heterogeneous batches, which in turn caused short interactive requests to stall behind head-of-line long requests. Root cause hypothesis: interaction between adaptive batching thresholds, the KV cache eviction policy, and our fair-dequeue heuristics produced backlog amplification and effective queue clogging for latency-sensitive flows. This ticket implements a two-part mitigation: 1) preemptive-dequeue path for latency-sensitive requests that permits safe early evacuation of short requests from pending batches via prioritized splitting, and 2) smoothing of KV-cache eviction pressure via an eviction-rate limiter + preferential cache pinning for short-session keys. Goals: stop customer-facing 99th token latency regressions, keep throughput loss < 5% for mixed workloads, validate on Hosted/Dedicated/Private matrix, and ship as runtime-1.22 canary.
comments: 2026-02-20 — Initial report from Support: Acme Health observed 3x 99th token latency vs baseline after weekend traffic shift. Incident assigned to eng on-call.

2026-02-21 — Repro: Marco reproduced long-tail locally with a mixed workload harness (short chat requests + long summarization requests) using private config. Capture traces: /confluence/serving/runtime/ENG-63321/traces (internal).

2026-02-24 — Investigation: Identified that adaptive batching allowed 2 large batches to coalesce because inter-arrival timers expired while long-context requests were enqueued. KV cache churn noted: heavy eviction spikes coincident with batch flushes. Logged as hypothesis in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/ENG-63321+design

2026-03-01 — Design review: Decided on preemptive-dequeue + bounded-split approach rather than full preemption to limit correctness risk. Agreed on metrics: per-tenant 99th token latency, batch composition entropy, throughput delta. Action: Marco to prototype split logic; Anika to draft rollout plan and monitors.

2026-03-04 — Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4881 — implements prioritized-split and a per-queue token-bucket to cap eviction rate. Benchmark harness run: mixed workload 50k samples, 99th token latency reduced by 62% for short requests, throughput drop 2.8%.

2026-03-07 — Review feedback: Security asked for additional validation for cache pinning to avoid data leakage across tenants — added explicit tenant-scoped pins and added audit log events. Compliance reviewed and approved the change set for Private deployments.

2026-03-09 — Canary plan: deploy runtime-1.22-canary to two Dedicated pools and one Private customer (Acme replica), with 4-hour escalations and automatic rollback on >10% P99 increase. Monitoring dashboards: /console/dashboards/runtime/ENG-63321-canary

2026-03-11 — Canary started at 02:30 UTC. Early signals: short-request P99 down 55% on canary pools, KV eviction rate smoothed; no correctness regressions found in structured output tests. Continuing observation window for 72 hours before staged rollout.
